definition: The component of the contact force from a surface that acts perpendicular to the surface, pushing on the body; it equals the weight only in special cases, such as a body at rest on level ground with no other vertical forces.
The component of the contact force parallel to a surface, opposing the sliding of the two surfaces or their tendency to slide.
A number with no unit that links friction to the normal force: static friction is at most $\mu_\text{s}F_\text{N}$, and sliding friction equals $\mu_\text{d}F_\text{N}$.
The pulling force a taut string, rope or cable exerts on a body attached to it, acting along the string away from the body.
The force a spring exerts is proportional to its extension and opposite to it, $F_\text{H} = -kx$, as long as the limit of proportionality is not passed.
The force per unit extension of a spring, $k$, in $\text{N m}^{-1}$; a stiffer spring has a larger spring constant.
The resistive force on a small sphere moving slowly through a fluid, opposite to its velocity, given by $F_\text{d} = 6\pi\eta r v$.
The upward force a fluid exerts on a body in it, equal to the weight of fluid displaced, $F_\text{b} = \rho V g$ with $\rho$ the density of the fluid.
The gravitational force on a body, $F_\text{g} = mg$, measured in newtons; unlike mass, it depends on the gravitational field strength where the body is.
The force between charged bodies, or on a charge in an electric field, whether or not the charge moves; like charges repel and unlike charges attract.
The force a magnetic field exerts on a moving charge or a current-carrying wire, perpendicular to both the velocity (or current) and the field.
